A big part of an investor's job is making founders more ambitious

"Pat Grady (@gradypb) was at our board meeting and we presented an extremely aggressive plan for next year in terms of hiring goals, commercial goals, product goals.

He goes, 'Gabe, if everyone in finance is gonna make a buying decision on AI in the next 18 months, and they are definitely gonna buy something no matter what, even if you're not there, then the only thing that matters is that you can blitz the market as quickly as possible to make sure that you are there. Given that, do you think this plan is aggressive enough or no?'

The answer was no. 

And the reason it wasn't aggressive enough is because I was being soft. 

My goal as a venture-backed business is to increase the tails of the distribution. It's fine if it gets 30% more likelihood that I fail if the odds that I become a $100 billion company also increase by 20%.

But you actually have to be okay with raising both of those tails at the same time."

tweets.text:
30,000 devices compromised across 100+ countries.

If a recruiter ever reaches out to you and it seems to good to be true, this is how you stay safe

1. Never run interview code on the computer holding your wallets or work credentials.

2. Use a disposable virtual machine for coding tests. Don’t connect your password manager, wallet, cloud accounts or shared folders.

3. Verify the recruiter independently. Find the company’s real website and contact them through an official address, not the details sent by the recruiter.

4. Don’t blindly run NPM projects or commands copied from an interview chat.

5. Treat “paste this command to fix the call” as a major red flag.

6. Open unknown VS Code projects in Restricted Mode. Click “No” when asked whether you trust the author.

7. Inspect .vscode/tasks.json, package scripts and install scripts before running anything.

8. Be suspicious of commands containing curl, wget, base64, -enc, mshta, iwr, Invoke-WebRequest or hidden execution. These can be legitimate, but not when an unknown recruiter pressures you to run them.

9. Keep seed phrases offline and keep wallet extensions off your development machine whenever possible.

10. Use short-lived credentials, hardware security keys and separate accounts for development, work and crypto.

#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold

⚡ DAILY METALS PULSE | 23 September 2026

🌍 Macro: Oil retreated Tuesday as Middle East supply flows improved, offering some relief on inflation. But the Fed’s latest rate hike and a firm dollar remain headwinds. This week’s Trump–Xi talks add another catalyst: trade relations matter directly for manufacturing, investment and metals demand.

☢️ Uranium: Washington and Seoul are discussing up to EIGHT new U.S. nuclear reactors, including six AP1000s and two Korean APR1400s. These projects still require agreements and execution, but they could underpin decades of additional fuel demand. Every credible reactor project strengthens the argument for securing uranium supplies early.

🥈 Silver: Silver futures edged higher Tuesday while gold slipped. Beyond the daily moves, AI infrastructure and grid investment support consumption, although solar manufacturers are reducing silver use. The Silver Institute’s 2026 outlook projects a supply deficit even with softer industrial demand—a reminder that demand needn’t break records for the market to remain undersupplied.

🥉 Copper: Chinese buying ahead of the holidays helped extend gains to a sixth session Tuesday. Shanghai exchange inventories have dropped around 70% since early June. Physical availability is tightening in China, while tariff uncertainty continues to redirect metal between markets. I’m watching whether buying stays strong after the holidays.

🟡 Gold: Tuesday’s modest decline shows the dollar still matters. Lower oil could ease inflation pressure if sustained, but the next bullish catalyst would be a meaningful easing in monetary conditions. That remains something to watch, rather than assume.

My view: the long-term metals case remains compelling. Tight financing makes strong balance sheets and the ability to deliver production especially valuable.

🗡️ What DeFi Shipped 🚢 (Sept 23):

Circle launched its own L1, and Aave and Compound both built doors for institutional money.

Here are 14 big updates in under a minute:

• @Arc, the L1 from @circle, went live. TVL (which could be rented) looks solid, but the reception across CT was poor.

• @aave proposed custodied collateral lending with @Anchorage holding the collateral. Institutions could borrow stablecoins against Bitcoin that never leaves regulated custody.

• @Compound_xyz opened its Institutional Market for USDC borrowing, with LTVs up to 87% on ETH, 85% on wstETH, and 81% on wBTC and cbBTC.

• @pendle_fi went live on Robinhood Chain with yield markets on tokenized stock dividends, starting with NVDA maturing October 15 and PFE maturing December 10.

• @Uniswap shipped StablePair Hook, a v4 hook that sets LP fees based on how far a pool has drifted from its reference rate. Live on two Ethereum pools, USDC/USDT and USDC/USDG.

• @base published the spec for Validity Transactions, which the chain includes only when onchain conditions match, gated on balance, storage, block number, or Flashblock index.

• @MetaMask now auto-reverts a transaction when real execution doesn't match what the wallet simulated. It targets "red pill" attacks, where a contract behaves one way in simulation and another onchain.

• @Pumpfun replaced Cashback Mode with Holder Rewards. Holder Reward tokens now pay out just for holding, with higher ceilings the longer you hold.

• @LidoFinance and @Stakely_io opened a public ETH staking vault built on stVaults, pairing ETH staking with the EarnETH DeFi strategy.

• @RenzoAI launched Renzo Basis, an automated delta-neutral basis trade on @HyperliquidX supporting BTC and HYPE at launch.

• @zama scaled up confidential DeFi with 16 yield vaults across five institutional curators, covering USDC, USDT, WBTC, AUSD, and tGBP, all deployed on @Morpho.

• @0xMiden, the privacy-focused chain incubated by @0xPolygon, shipped testnet v0.16, the last major release before mainnet.

• @DeriveXYZ proposed V3, a zkVM exchange settling on Ethereum L1. The matching engine and sequencer state transitions get proved in a zkVM, with user funds custodied in L1 contracts.

• @verantaxyz, the leveraged-trading protocol on @base, rebranded from Avantis and dropped its invite-code gate.

I’m fine with institutions keeping their custodians and compliance teams bc that’s probably what it takes to get them comfortable using DeFi.

I just don’t want that to become the only way to use it. I’d still like to borrow against my holdings at 2 a.m. without asking someone for permission.

I actually wrote about this a couple years ago - due to failures of modern education and degree inflation it was clear that trade schools and trade professions would be more valuable - learning how to do things 

Then the Palantir Internship came out that basically got students into Palantir out of high school. And that is IMO where the world will be heading - we're basically back to Industrial Era type style of modern education

Apprenticeship - just that now not at a blacksmith, but rather, at the largest companies in the world. It was obvious that the next thing to do was build your own school - and tie it to your company

Obviously, the last stage will be give them housing too - and now you have basically successfully, from first-principles, re-invented countries, and the previous era of humanity. 

Soon you will be able to sign up to Elon Musk University, where you will be given a dorm, and then you can work at one of the Elon companies. And then repeated for all the major companies in the world.

I don't really know whether this is good or bad. Probably both. Anyways, all the outcome of a K shaped world.
